criteria.description: Fidelity to body: every factual claim in the abstract must be supported sentence-by-sentence by the body. Defects include invented or misattributed facts, merging results from different objects, upgrading ongoing/future work to completed results, adding numeric ranges or percentages not present in the body, and omitting caveats the body states about the approximation.

Coverage of problem, method, and findings: abstract must state the problem (Pauli depolarizing channel poorly approximates non-unital channels like amplitude damping), the method (expanding to efficiently simulable Clifford and Pauli-measurement-induced translation channels: PC, CC, PMC, CMC, selecting best valid approximation with smaller fidelity than target by minimizing Hilbert-Schmidt distance), and the comparative findings (adding Clifford and/or measurement errors improves accuracy, CMC best, with compact distribution and many random channels approximated closely).

Appropriate uncertainty and validity: abstract must not overstate results, must reflect the validity condition (approximation has smaller fidelity than target) and that improvements are shown for the tested amplitude damping and random channels, without claiming universal logical error-rate results which are listed as future work.

Coherent abstract structure and length compliance: abstract is a single coherent paragraph of approximately 113 words, covering problem-method-findings in order, and must not exceed target by more than ~30% (about 147 words). Tokenization spacing artifacts from source must be treated as minor presentation only, not as content errors.
